raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

- DeepSeek-V4.1 has an option called decoder bounded replay (`--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`). When it is on, the last layers of the model only process the last 128 prompt tokens of each request during prefill.
- Today this starts at layer 21. Layer 20 still processes every prompt token.
- Layer 20 does two things. It writes the compressed KV cache that decoding reads later, and that needs every token. It also runs its own indexer, attention and MoE to produce its output, and layer 21 only reads the last 128 tokens of that output.
- So the indexer, attention and MoE work of layer 20 on all the earlier tokens is thrown away. The indexer of layer 20 scans the whole context, so this wasted work grows with the prompt length.

## Modifications

- When decoder bounded replay is on, layer 20 now writes its compressed KV cache for every token first, and then runs the rest of the layer on the last 128 tokens only.
- The compressed KV cache that layer 20 writes is the same as before.
- Layer 20 now writes its indexer results directly for the last 128 tokens. The code that copied those rows out of the full-size buffers is no longer needed, so this PR removes it.
- No flag is added. Nothing changes when decoder bounded replay is off.
- ROCm keeps the old behavior, because its fused layer path runs all of layer 20 in one call.

One behavior change to review:

- For the last 128 tokens, layer 20 now uses the same shortened sliding window as layers 21 to 39. Before this PR, layer 20 saw the full window.
- This matches how the DeepSeek-V4.1 report describes decoder replay: "feed their encoder outputs through the decoder layers under the same SWA truncation".

## Accuracy Tests

- Hardware and model: 4x B300, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP4 and EP4.
- "main" is commit `2f6e0ec45d`. The two files this PR changes are the same on current main.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 16 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay
# The DSpark row adds: --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1319 --parallel 32
```

| GSM8K, 1319 questions | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No speculative decoding | 0.907 | 0.907 |
| DSpark, block size 5 | 0.902 | 0.914 |

- Each number is one run. Two runs of the same setup can differ by about 0.007.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Same launch command as above, without speculative decoding.
- The numbers are time to first token. Requests are sent one at a time, as token ids.
- Each number is the median of 3 to 5 requests. The two numbers in a cell come from two separate server starts.

| Request | main | this PR | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New prompt, 16K tokens | 139.6 / 139.5 ms | 132.8 / 131.6 ms | 5% faster |
| New prompt, 64K tokens | 577.5 / 564.9 ms | 526.6 / 524.5 ms | 8% faster |
| New prompt, 200K tokens | 2009.6 / 2015.4 ms | 1800.5 / 1811.9 ms | 10% faster |
| New prompt, 500 to 8K tokens | 81.7 to 85.7 ms | 82.5 to 84.4 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 16K cached tokens | 85.8 / 87.2 ms | 84.4 / 85.5 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 64K cached tokens | 93.5 / 89.4 ms | 93.2 / 91.4 ms | No change |
| 2K new tokens after 200K cached tokens | 112.4 / 113.9 ms | 115.2 / 113.3 ms | No change |
| 128 new tokens after 200K cached tokens | 109.3 / 107.8 ms | 114.2 / 113.0 ms | 5 ms slower |

Time spent in layer 20 for one 16K-token prefill chunk, measured with a GPU sync around each layer:

| Prefill chunk | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Early in the prompt | 11.9 ms | 3.3 ms |
| Late in a 200K-token prompt | 27.0 ms | 5.2 ms |

- Short requests do not get faster. Prefill without a CUDA graph costs about 80 ms per batch no matter how short the prompt is, and this PR does not change that.
- The last row of the first table is the only one that got slower. In a third pair of server starts it was 109.2 ms on main and 107.3 ms with this PR, so I think it is noise between server starts.

## Not tested

- Prefill context parallelism together with decoder bounded replay.
- ROCm. Its behavior is unchanged.

## Follow-up

- `CandidateMetadata.tail` and its implementations are now only called by their own tests. A later PR can remove them.
